claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child - my 14-year-old, Alex. We're currently living abroad, but I wanted to check if I might still be able to claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 14 years old, and you're currently living abroad.

Before I assess your eligibility, I need to understand your residency situation better:

**Are you a British citizen, and what is your current immigration status in the country where you're living?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen. We're living overseas at the moment - I moved abroad for work about a year ago. Alex is with me here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I need to check the specific rules about Child Benefit eligibility for people living abroad. Let me review the official guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, I can see there's a section on living abroad. The guidance states that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant. I need to know more about your specific situation:

**Which country are you currently living in with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're living in Spain at the moment. I took a job with a private company out here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your work situation and whether you maintain ties to the UK:

**Are you currently paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, or are you paying social security contributions in Spain through your employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm paying social security contributions in Spain through my job here - that's what my employer set up when I moved.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I need to check the detailed rules about living abroad and eligibility, as this is important for your case.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see the guidance mentions that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant. However, the information I have states that normally you need to be living in the UK to qualify. Since you're living in Spain and paying Spanish social security contributions rather than UK National Insurance, I need to clarify one more important detail:

**Do you have British citizenship with the right to reside in Spain, or are you there under a specific visa arrangement?** (This helps determine if there are any reciprocal social security agreements that might apply.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have British citizenship and I'm living in Spain under the post-Brexit residency rules - I registered and got my residency card when I moved there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Let me review the detailed eligibility information more carefully to understand the specific rules for British citizens living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official government guidance I've reviewed, I can now provide you with your eligibility assessment for Child Benefit.

The key rule is that you **normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK**. The guidance states that you "may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries," but the specific circumstances for this are limited and typically involve Crown servants or certain reciprocal social security arrangements.

As a British citizen living in Spain and paying Spanish social security contributions rather than UK National Insurance, the standard rules indicate that you would not qualify for Child Benefit, as the basic eligibility requirement is to live in the UK.

However, I should note that the government website suggests contacting the Child Benefit Office directly for clarification on your specific circumstances, as there may be additional considerations related to social security agreements between the UK and Spain, or other exceptional circumstances that could apply to your case.

Based on the official Child Benefit eligibility rules, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** under the current circumstances.

That said, I'd encourage you to **contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly** to discuss your specific situation. They may be able to advise whether any reciprocal social security agreements between the UK and Spain, or other exceptional circumstances, might apply to your case. Sometimes there are arrangements that aren't immediately apparent from the main eligibility guidance.
